episode_title: Ep. 52: The Future of Aging, AI, and Robotics with CEO of Insilico Medicine - Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD

real_qa.q: What is Alex Zhavoronkov's background before founding Insilico Medicine?
real_qa.r: Zhavoronkov earned his first two degrees in computer science and commerce from Queen's University in Canada, worked for semiconductor companies including ATI Technologies which led in GPU technology, and later completed graduate work at Johns Hopkins University in biotechnology, mathematics, and target discovery. He worked for multiple biotechs, ran his own lab in regenerative medicine and bioinformatics, and attended NVIDIA GTC conferences starting in 2012-2013 where he presented on deep learning for drug discovery and aging research.

real_qa.q: How does Insilico Medicine use deep learning to predict biological aging?
real_qa.r: Insilico Medicine trains deep neural networks on multiple biological data types simultaneously—gene expression, protein expression, and methylation—to predict a universal feature that connects all humans: age. By treating biological data like a continuous video flow, the AI learns patterns and connections between previously disconnected data types. Zhavoronkov published his first aging clock using deep learning in 2016, which connects previously disconnected biological data into models that understand aging in time.
real_qa.requete: Insilico Medicine aging clock deep learning

real_qa.q: What regulatory framework ensures AI-designed drugs meet safety and efficacy standards?
real_qa.r: The FDA provides clear regulatory standards that apply equally regardless of drug discovery method or company background. Every drug must be proven safe and effective, and the FDA will not approve drugs without rigorous evidence of safety and efficacy. Once submitted to the FDA for human clinical trials, applications undergo rigorous review, and drugs must demonstrate safety and tolerability over extended periods in healthy volunteers before testing in patients through double-blind placebo-controlled trials, just like any other technology.
real_qa.requete: FDA AI drug discovery safety regulations approval

real_qa.q: How quickly can Insilico Medicine move from drug discovery to human clinical trials?
real_qa.r: Insilico Medicine has achieved an average time to preclinical candidate of 13 months and an average time to human clinical trial of about two years or even lower from zero. This compares to the previous timeline of four to six years for traditional drug discovery, accomplished with higher degree of novelty through industrializing and optimizing the entire discovery process.
real_qa.requete: Insilico Medicine timeline drug discovery clinical trials months

real_qa.q: What is Insilico Medicine's strategy for making AI drug discovery globally accessible?
real_qa.r: Zhavoronkov emphasizes democratization of AI technology through cell phones that can provide university-level capabilities to developing nations in Africa and Southeast Asia. He advocates for building drug discovery programs in developing countries and wealthy nations in the Middle East seeking to diversify beyond oil. He notes that global collaboration with regulators could accelerate drug development in rare diseases and explore geographic advantages, such as running rare disease studies in China or India where large electronically-connected populations enable quick patient recruitment.
real_qa.requete: Insilico Medicine global drug discovery developing countries
